title: SCE Schedule TOU-GS-2, Option E — Time-of-Use, General Service, Demand Metered, 20-200 kW
notes:
Transcribed directly from fixtures/tariff-sheets/ELECTRIC_SCHEDULES_TOU-GS-2.pdf (21 pages) by Claude. Bundled Service only — Direct Access and CCA Service customers pay Delivery per this record but Generation per their own provider (Sheet 12, Special Condition 12), so the "generation"-component lines here do not apply to them (CLAUDE.md: be explicit about which component a recommendation affects).

IMPORTANT CORRECTION to earlier secondary-source-based assumption: Option E is NOT "FRD only, no TRD." Its DELIVERY-side Time Related Demand rate is $0.00/kW (so no delivery TRD line is billed — omitted here rather than included as a permanent $0 line), but a NONZERO GENERATION-side time-related demand rate still applies for Bundled Service Customers: $5.65/kW Summer On-Peak, $2.18/kW Winter Mid-Peak (Sheet 5 Rates table, UG column). So Option E DOES have a real, billable time-related demand charge — just only on the generation component, not delivery. This changes the structural framing used in packages/rating-engine/test/option-structure.test.ts and PENDING.md, both written before this PDF was read.

KNOWN BUT NOT MODELED (all require account/election-conditional logic this schema does not yet support — flagged in PENDING.md, not silently dropped):
- TOU Option Meter Charge (RTEM), $40.79/meter/month — Sheet 4/5 Rates, Special Condition 2. Only applies if the customer elects an RTEM meter.
- California Climate Credit, -$36.00/meter — Sheet 13, Special Condition 13. Applied ONLY on April and October bills, only for "Small Business Customers" (billing demand did not exceed 20 kW in more than three of the preceding twelve months), applied after city/county utility users' taxes and before franchise fees. Needs month-conditional rider support the engine does not have.
- Single Phase Service credit, -$9.30/month — Sheet 4/5 Rates, Special Condition 7. Conditional on the account being single-phase-metered; ServiceAttributes has no phase field yet.
- Voltage Discounts (Facilities/TRD/Energy), tiered from 2 kV to 220 kV — Sheet 4/5 Rates, Special Condition 8. Every tier starts at 2 kV; a v1 customer at standard secondary voltage (<2 kV) gets no discount at all, so this is expected to be irrelevant for the target audience, not merely unmodeled.
- CARE Discount (32.5%) and Food Bank Discount (20%) — Sheet 12/20, Special Conditions 11 and 16. Both require an enrollment/eligibility declaration form; no such account flag exists yet.
- City/county Utility Users' Tax and franchise fees — NOT part of this schedule at all (Sheet 13 only references their existence and ordering relative to the Climate Credit). These are jurisdiction-specific and must come from a separate, city-specific rider once the customer's city is known.

BILLING DEMAND ROUNDING — Sheet 11, Special Condition 6: "The Billing Demand shall be the kW of Maximum Demand, determined to the nearest kW." The engine currently does NOT round a demand charge's billed kW to an integer before applying the rate; it only rounds the resulting DOLLAR amount to cents. This is a real discrepancy against real bills and needs an engine change (a rounding step on billedKw), not a data fill — flagged in PENDING.md, not implemented here.

demandRules.label: Reached 200 kW in any three months of the preceding twelve
demandRules.citation: Verified from fixtures/tariff-sheets/ELECTRIC_SCHEDULES_TOU-GS-2.pdf, Sheet 1 — Applicability: "The Customer whose monthly Maximum Demand, in the opinion of SCE, is expected to reach 200 kW or has reached 200 kW for any three months during the preceding 12 months is ineligible for service under this Schedule. Effective with the date of ineligibility, the Customer's account shall be transferred to Schedule TOU-GS-3." windowIncludesCurrentMonth=false is Claude's reading of the word "preceding" (before the current month) — an interpretation of ambiguous natural language, not a transcribed number. PLEASE CONFIRM: does the month being billed count toward the three, or only the twelve months strictly before it?.

demandRules.label: At or below 20 kW for twelve consecutive months
demandRules.citation: Verified from fixtures/tariff-sheets/ELECTRIC_SCHEDULES_TOU-GS-2.pdf, Sheet 1 — Applicability: "Any Customer served under this Schedule whose monthly Maximum Demand has registered 20 kW or less for 12 consecutive months will be transferred to Schedule TOU-GS-1." windowIncludesCurrentMonth=true is Claude's reading: unlike the 200 kW rule above, this sentence has no "preceding" qualifier, so the most recently billed month is read as the 12th of the 12 consecutive — an interpretation, not a transcribed number. PLEASE CONFIRM..

timeRelated.label: Time Related Demand Charge - Summer Season, On-Peak (Generation)
timeRelated.citation: Verified from fixtures/tariff-sheets/ELECTRIC_SCHEDULES_TOU-GS-2.pdf, Sheet 5 — Rates table, "Time Related Demand Charge - Summer Season, On-Peak" row, UG column. weekdaysOnly=false: this charge's own TOU period (summer On-Peak) is already weekday-only per Sheet 8's table (On-Peak is N/A on weekends/holidays in every season), so there is no separate restriction to apply -- and, consistent with that, the rate table carries no "(Weekdays)" label on this row, unlike the winter Mid-Peak row. See the winter Mid-Peak charge's citation for the genuine ambiguity that does not apply here.

timeRelated.label: Time Related Demand Charge - Winter Season, Mid-Peak (Generation)
timeRelated.citation: GENUINELY AMBIGUOUS between two sections of fixtures/tariff-sheets/ELECTRIC_SCHEDULES_TOU-GS-2.pdf. Sheet 8, Special Condition 1's TOU period table defines winter Mid-Peak as 4pm-9pm on EVERY day, weekday or weekend/holiday alike (the table shows "4 p.m. - 9 p.m." under both the Weekday-Winter and Weekend/Holiday-Winter cells for Mid-Peak). But Sheet 4 (Option D) and Sheet 5 (Option E) both label the winter TRD rate row itself "Mid-peak - Weekdays (4-9pm)", and the corresponding voltage-discount row "Voltage Discount, Winter Weekday Mid-Peak" -- the SAME weekday-specific label, on both options, appearing nowhere else (summer On-Peak's TRD row carries no such label, because its period is already weekday-only, so the label would be redundant there -- its selective presence here reads as deliberate). Special Condition 6 (Billing Demand) does not resolve this: it says TRD is measured "during ... each of the TOU Periods" with no weekday carve-out of its own, so it is silent on whether the rate table's narrower label overrides the period's own definition. weekdaysOnly=true is the chosen interpretation (matching the rate table's specific, twice-repeated label over the general period table), NOT a resolved fact -- the engine computes both readings and warns if they would measure a different peak. PLEASE CONFIRM which section governs.

riders.citation: Verified from fixtures/tariff-sheets/ELECTRIC_SCHEDULES_TOU-GS-2.pdf, Sheet 5 — Rates table footnote 12: "recovers the net cost associated with system reliability procurement... on behalf of customers whose generation services are provided by certain Electric Service Providers or Community Choice Aggregators."
